forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

summary.summary: A short covering report to Audit Committee confirming that North Tyneside published its draft 2025/26 Statement of Accounts on 30 June 2026, meeting the statutory deadline. Forvis Mazars have been given the supporting working papers and detailed audit testing is underway as part of the sector-wide 'rebuilding assurance' process; the draft can be inspected until 20 August 2026 and the audited accounts must be approved and published by 31 January 2027. The paper itself carries no financial figures — the draft statement lives on the council's website, so the balance-sheet position must be read there.

signals.headline: Draft 2025/26 Statement of Accounts published 30 June 2026, on the statutory deadline; Forvis Mazars fieldwork underway and public inspection open until 20 August 2026
signals.why: On-time draft publication with the audit already in fieldwork supports a timely opinion ahead of the 31 January 2027 backstop — no slippage to watch here yet.

news_drafts.headline: North Tyneside expects £8.7m grant covering 90% of its schools funding deficit
news_drafts.lead:
North Tyneside Council expects an initial £8.7m payment on 30 November from the government's High Needs Stability Grant. The grant covers 90% of the council's deficit on the dedicated schools grant (DSG) up to the end of 2025/26. The DSG is the government grant that funds schools, and a deficit on it is an overspend, usually on support for children with special needs. The council's papers say the Department for Education confirmed in October that its Local Area Reform Plan submission was successful, which triggers the payment.

Cabinet's initial budget proposals for 2027/28 include £2.5m for the council's local contribution towards the remaining 10%, shown under Schools Support Services. The medium-term financial plan now carries that £2.5m as a contribution to a DSG cumulative deficit reserve. The paper says this has delayed the planned replenishment of the General Fund balance, which was originally included at £2.0m. The minimum General Fund balance is set at £7m.

The statutory override, a temporary government rule that keeps schools-funding deficits off councils' main balance sheets, is currently due to end on 31 March 2028. Unless it is extended, the paper says authorities will need to show they can cover DSG deficits from available reserves. The paper calls this a key risk for the council.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - 2027-2031 Financial Planning and Budget Process Cabinet 24 November
findings.headline: CIPFA referred to the Authority as being a clear outlier in some areas of expenditure when compared to the average spend of its statistical neighbours.
findings.detail: The paper says this comes from the CIPFA Resilience Review reported to Cabinet in June 2026. The paper cites higher than average spend on cultural and related services, including leisure, as an example.
findings.matters: A finance officer at another council would want to know how a CIPFA resilience review benchmarks spending against statistical neighbours.
findings.quote: CIPFA referred to the Authority as being a clear outlier in some areas of expenditure when compared to the average spend of its statistical neighbours.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - 2027-2031 Financial Planning and Budget Process Cabinet 24 November
findings.headline: HRA debt is expected to fall from £290.825m at self-financing to £224.89m at March 2027, with a reduction of £65.935m since the start of self-financing.
findings.detail: The paper says debt will be reduced to £132.281m by the end of the 30-year business plan, a £92.609m repayment over that period. Decisions to repay debt continue to be made within the Treasury Management Strategy.
findings.matters: A lender tracking HRA leverage would want to see the debt reduction and the repayment target over the business plan.
findings.figures: £290.825m opening self-financing debt; £224.89m expected HRA debt at March 2027; £65.935m reduction since self-financing; £132.281m closing debt after 30 years; £92.609m repaid over 30 years
findings.quote: having been reduced by £65.935m since the start of self-financing.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - 2027-2031 Financial Planning and Budget Process Cabinet 24 November
findings.headline: The General Fund plan assumes £64.965m of prudential borrowing, with capital financing costs of £18.422m in 2027/28 rising to £18.478m by 2031/32.
findings.detail: The paper says every £1m of borrowing costs about £0.1m per year in revenue. Financing costs are described as mostly relating to historic investment.
findings.matters: A lender or finance director would see the new borrowing requirement and the revenue cost it adds to the budget.
findings.figures: £64.965m prudential borrowing assumed; £18.422m capital financing costs 2027/28; £18.478m by 2031/32; £0.1m annual revenue cost per £1m borrowed
findings.quote: The proposed General Fund plan assumes £64.965m of prudential borrowing at this stage.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - 2027-2031 Financial Planning and Budget Process Cabinet 24 November
findings.headline: The proposed 2027-2031 Investment Plan is currently £385.547m, against £352.265m approved by Council in February 2026.
findings.detail: The paper says the plan was adjusted for reprofiling and additional funding allocations. The General Fund element is funded £78.609m from grants and contributions, with 54.8% of the General Fund programme externally funded.
findings.matters: A council or lender comparing capital programme size would want the change from the approved February plan and the share of grant funding.
findings.figures: £352.265m approved Investment Plan (February 2026); £385.547m current proposed plan; £78.609m General Fund grants and contributions; 54.8% of General Fund programme

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - 2027-2031 Financial Planning and Budget Process Cabinet 24 November
findings.headline: Maintained school deficits are described as currently in excess of £15m, with a risk the council would need to absorb the debt without action.
findings.detail: The paper says there are increasing levels of maintained school deficits and that the council would need to absorb this debt without action. The paper proposes a systematic review of the education system as the response.
findings.matters: A finance director would want to see the size of a school-deficit contingent liability that could fall to the council's own balance sheet.
findings.figures: in excess of £15m maintained school deficit
findings.quote: there is a risk we would need to absorb this debt, which is currently in excess of £15m
